name: Expanding Horizons
summary: Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine to Stormwind. He wants the settlement's work and its home known beyond Darkshore.

sections.title: Bridging Two Hemispheres
sections.body: Auberdine's sea passage now joins Darkshore directly to Stormwind. Its leaders want the shipping route kept safe and the coastal settlement linked to the wider Alliance. Nearby, the ruined cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran have long drawn more notice than Auberdine and its living people.

sections.title: A Missive to the City Architect
sections.body: Baros Alexston oversees Stormwind's construction and infrastructure. His duties include public works and logistics. Thundris Windweaver's letter crosses the Great Sea to the official charged with the human capital's building needs.

faq.q: Who sends you on this quest?
faq.answer: Thundris Windweaver, an influential night elf in Auberdine, asks you to carry his letter. He feels Darnassus and allies across the ocean overlook the settlement, and seeks a formal link with the human kingdom.
Baros Alexston is Stormwind's City Architect. A respected civic planner, he knew Edwin VanCleef when they were younger. He oversees construction and structural administration throughout the capital.

faq.q: Why is Auberdine reaching out to Stormwind?
faq.answer: Auberdine wants its harbor known as a gateway for supplies, commerce, and Alliance travel. Its leaders hope the new sea routes between Darkshore and the Eastern Kingdoms will strengthen economic and logistical ties with the human kingdom.

faq.q: How does travel work between Auberdine and Stormwind?
aliases: how to get to stormwind from auberdine
faq.answer: A vessel now sails from Auberdine across the Great Sea to Stormwind Harbor. It brings supplies and life to Auberdine's shores.

Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran were prosperous highborne cities in ancient Darkshore. The Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago. Now the cities lie in haunted ruins, more prominent in kaldorei history than living villages like Auberdine.

faq.q: Why deliver this to an architect instead of King Anduin or Bolvar?
faq.answer: Thundris Windweaver gives no reason for his choice. He asks you to take the letter to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect, so Auberdine's work can be recognized.

angles.text: For the kaldorei, opening sea routes to the Eastern Kingdoms ends ten thousand years of seclusion and binds your people to human civilization.
As a human, you see the rebuilt kingdom's reach grow when you return to Stormwind carrying a kaldorei settlement's seal.
As an Alliance member, you see the work needed to unite peoples across two continents in one faction.
